column3: the Ascent seen from far out on a grey ring-sea at dusk: a colossal slender tower made of a hundred stacked countries, each floor a paper-thin tray of landscape - a hairline of forest, a hairline of snowfield, a hairline of farmland - seen almost edge-on, with tall bands of open sky between the trays, clouds drifting freely through the gaps and casting shadows on the trays below, each tray held at its rim by needle-thin pillars and webs of fine triangular cables, one single thread-like climbing spine visible between two floors like spider silk, the lowest floors dark and grey under heavy cloud-lids, three or four floors higher up glowing warm gold where their gloom has lifted, the stack narrowing with haze as it rises and dissolving into the sky with no visible top, a tiny port town with lanterns and fishing boats at its foot for scale

bird's-eye map view of a ramshackle port town built from wreckage on the shore of a grey ring-sea at the foot of the Ascent, fishing boats and floating piers, a market square, an aether-forge beside a horse trough; one whole side of the map is the tower's footing - a forest of colossal needle-thin black pillars rising out of the top of the frame, webbed with fine triangular cables, and high above the town the dark underside of the lowest hanging country cutting across the sky like a stormfront with one thread-thin stair-spine descending from it to a hill-tall gate arch that dwarfs the tiny houses, no iron wall, no cliff, no nautical anchors
a plain military banner with a simple shield-wall emblem of interlocked shields, hanging worn and carefully mended from a wooden pole, plain background, no lettering on the cloth
the underside of a stolen country rising into a night sky - torn earth, roots, cellars and lamplit windows hanging above a dark field, watched from below by a small boy alone in the stubble

a weathered woman drilling raw recruits with spears in a muddy shantytown yard, morning fog, a carved stone of names behind her; behind and above the fog the horizon is a forest of impossibly tall thin black pillars webbed with slanting cables, rising out of the top of the frame, and high above them the dark underside of a whole hanging country cuts across the sky like a stormfront, faint lamps glimmering on its underside, no wall, no masonry, no stone blocks

a queue of medieval climbers at dawn before a black iron gate arch at the foot of a thread-thin climbing spire that rises out of the top of the frame toward the dark underside of a country hanging in the sky, needle-thin pillars and triangular cables in the haze behind, one crystal splinter blazing with light above a woman's outstretched palm while the crowd turns to look; the crowd in hooded cloaks, wool tunics and shawls carrying wicker packs, bedrolls and satchels, strictly medieval - no modern backpacks, no caps or hats with brims, no modern clothing, no stone blocks, not masonry

hedged farmland in old straight lines stretching to a far horizon under a vast pale shadowless sky of sourceless false daylight, no sun visible, a grey wolf slipping through a hedge gap in the foreground, hay-ricks going grey in the pale paper-colored grass, an eerie flat noon that never ends
a goblin king slumped on a makeshift throne of crates and banner-poles, crown askew, surrounded by a hundred stolen tattered banners in a muster meadow, a small goblin cup-bearer at the throne's foot
a heavy toll-chain slung across a carved stair-lift arch in living rock, coins nailed to a wooden post, armed toll-keepers half in shadow

a giantess's huge scarred open palm on which lies a heavy hinged iron slave collar with a crude lock plate and a short length of broken chain, her other thumb pointing at a tiny maker's forge-mark stamped in the flat of the metal, dim smithy interior with anvil and hanging tongs behind, fully monochrome graphite, no fire visible, absolutely not a ring, not held between fingers
a night battle in a vast mine gallery - lantern light and war drums, siege ladders against a stockade of tents and bone totems, iron cages cracked open, gaunt prisoners walking out through the smoke

a one-armed veteran in a patched gambeson and mail, his empty sleeve pinned at the shoulder, holding out a mended much-patched banner to a kneeling woman commander in worn plate armor, before a silent crowd of gaunt freed prisoners among ruined medieval tents, no modern clothing of any kind
an abandoned fairground - empty prize cages, torn bunting streaming in wind, a carousel of carved wolves, not one living soul
a scarred veteran kneeling in a dark silk-hung cavern among cocooned shapes of armored soldiers, his sword driven point-down into the ground beside him

three medieval armies' banners tangled in a melee on grassy burial mounds as the mounds crack open and grey shrouded figures rise out of the earth, soldiers in mail and kettle helms with spears and round shields, overcast daylight only, strictly medieval fantasy - no modern lighting, no electric lights, no fluorescent tubes

a hundred climbers kneeling in ranks at the edge of a moat around a great burial mound at dusk, ravens circling; on the mound's crest stands a drowned king - a heavy broad-shouldered figure in waterlogged grave-robes and a tarnished round crown grown over with moss, his face hidden behind a hanging funeral veil of threaded coins

an immense elegant true spider - fully arachnid, no human face or torso - enthroned on a vast web hung with tribute: lanterns, armor, harps and lutes; she delicately holds a tiny steaming teacup in one raised foreleg, an elf archer standing small in the silk below, web-vaulted cavern hall
an elf and a vast graceful spider playing a game of knotted silk threads by lamplight in a web-vaulted hall, both concentrating
a grey-cloaked elf woman standing on a misty tree-lined bridleway, crows lining the branches above her, her face unreadable
a stone wall covered in thousands of chalked names in many scripts, a small goblin on a ladder adding one more name, refugee campfires below

a medieval army with ox-drawn sledge-trains crossing a frozen sea past tall wooden sailing ships locked keel-over in the pack ice, brine gulls wheeling, soldiers wrapped in wool cloaks, furs and mail with spears and shields on the sledges, strictly medieval fantasy - no parkas, no modern polar expedition gear, no goggles, no rifles
two giants arguing across a glowing light-table that projects a cross-section schematic of a tower of stacked lands, their shadows huge on the workshop wall

an immense ancient wyrm coiled around drifts of grey ash in a volcanic caldera at night, its huge head lowered level with a tiny woman seated at a small campfire before it, the wyrm's eyes half-lidded and weary with great age, smoke rising from distant vents, an air of geologic patience rather than menace
a single-file line of shuttered lanterns crossing a dark dust plain pocked with funnel-pits and hidden trapdoor lids, a small goblin walking point with a staff
a vast timber mead-hall packed with a parliament of men, giants, elves and goblins arguing across trestle tables, a hundred banners hung from the rafters, hearth-light
a great mead-hall burning at night - rafters of banners aflame, two far doorways each held by a lone fighter against shadows, people fleeing out into the snow between them
six empty chairs around a scorched council table in a burnt-out hall, morning light falling through the broken roof onto the ash
soldiers walking single file along a mile-long mooring chain slung between floating islands, cloud far below, sky-wrecks hanging in the links
an army blown off a cloud-wreathed ridgeline by a colossal gale, banners and soldiers scattered into the sky like seed, a regal storm-queen watching from a throne of wind and lightning
an elf archer breaking a carved wooden token over his knee before a delegation of hooded elven envoys, his jaw set, their faces cold
an army asleep in a perfect circle of uncanny calm inside a towering ring of standing rain, one small goblin awake and listening, distant horns implied by rising birds

a woman walking alone and empty-handed toward a wall of pale hounds and mounted hunters robed in bone-pale hooded hunting garb crowned with antlers, in a night forest clearing, her dropped sword behind her in the leaves, medieval fantasy, no hats, no modern clothing
a trophy wall of hundreds of captured shields in a pale antlered hunting court, one battered shield picked out by a shaft of light

a woman alone at a watch-fire on a black iron anchor-platform at a floor's rim at night, a glowing crystal splinter in her open palm, behind her nothing but open air: moonlit cloud-tops far below her feet, the thin glowing hairline of another whole country hanging in the darkness beneath the clouds, fine cables rising past her catching the starlight, the dark underside of the land above cutting across the top of the frame, wind in her cloak, no battlements, no masonry, no iron wall
an army mustered in ranks at the foot of black iron outworks, green stolen country falling away behind them, riveted industrial darkness rising ahead

medieval sappers in mail coifs, kettle helms and gambesons prying at a riveted iron rampart with pry-bars beneath wooden mantlets, a section of living iron wall rearing out of the rampart above them, grappling chains and torch smoke, strictly medieval - no modern military helmets, no firearms, no metal barrels
a welded soldier with human eyes above an iron jaw standing very still before a woman commander who has recognized him, welding gantries and chain hoists behind
a small leather cipher-book with blood on the page margins, held open in two careful hands, council chamber out of focus behind
a vast battle before an iron gate beneath a drum-throne - mid-charge, thousands of iron collars bursting from soldiers' necks in a rippling wave of light that crosses the field like frost cracking
an empty giant gauntlet clutching a broken chain on the steps of a silent drum-throne, fallen banners settling around it

four medieval fantasy climbers ascending a black mirror-glass stair above clouds - a woman fighter in scale armor, a tall elf archer with a bow, a huge giant in smith's leathers, a small goblin - and in the glass their four reflections do not match them: standing straighter, crueler, colder, dressed in finer darker versions of their clothes; strictly medieval fantasy, no modern clothing or gear
a giant's hand resting on a great thrown lever in a reactor gallery, colorless light dying away down long vaulted halls of coil and lead

a tall woman in ancient dented plate armor of an old fashion stepping out of a black adamant door, offering a longsword hilt-first to a kneeling weathered woman commander with cropped hair, freed captives watching from the torchlit dark behind; entirely original faces resembling no actor or film character

a vast engine-hall seen from behind a throne that is part of the tower's machinery - a high seat welded from boiler-plate, pistons, chain-gears and ledger-shelves built into its arms, absolutely not made of swords or blades; one gaunt crowned figure seated alone, and at the far doors a world of peoples pouring in with banners and lamplight

a market square in a gate-town at dawn, recruits drilling with spears, a mended banner leaning against a horse trough in the foreground; above the rooftops there is no open sky - the whole heaven is the smooth dark underside of the country hanging above, a vast lid across the world faintly washed with sourceless pale light, and at the far end of one street a low blinding blade of true golden dawn light rakes in sideways from the distant rim, quiet and still, not masonry, no stone blocks, no iron wall

an old veteran soldier in a patched gambeson seated on a log by a night campfire, shown from his left side so his empty left sleeve, folded flat and pinned up at the shoulder, faces the viewer plainly - there is no left arm, only the pinned sleeve - while his right hand works a needle through a worn grey banner spread over his knee, a kneeling woman in mail pulling the cloth taut, a small goblin and two gaunt soldiers listening across the fire, the banner bearing a stitched dry-stone wall with one crooked star, burnt black heathland running to a far horizon under an enormous starless sky, strictly medieval

a heavy older merchant in a singed travelling coat carrying two iron strong-boxes strapped to his back in a wooden porter's frame, scorched ledgers clamped under one arm, trudging on foot up a rutted gate road toward armed medieval pickets at dusk, a few soot-stained clerks trailing him, the toll-road behind running to the horizon of a vast flat country where one thin column of smoke stands up into an enormous grey sky

a small goblin with a tall banner-pole standing before a giant standing-stone carved with dense columns of small names, a stonemason on a wooden ladder chiselling a tiny doorway-shaped mark beside one of the names, no glowing letters, no legible words, a dawn queue of grain wagons and young spear-carrying recruits waiting behind them; above the rooftops the whole sky is the smooth dark underside of the country hanging above, a vast lid faintly washed with pale sourceless light, one thread-thin climbing spine dropping from it to the horizon, strictly medieval - no modern clothing or gear, no iron wall

a huge giantess blacksmith at an anvil in a timber smithy, forge-welding two small pieces of iron into one glowing bar while a young couple stand close in the heat holding hands, deep snow outside the open smithy door and a vast lamplit timber mead-hall beyond, wedding guests of many peoples - men, giants, elves, kobolds - crowded warm in the doorway in wool and furs, strictly medieval fantasy - no modern clothing, no modern tools, no firearms

a vast vaulted storm-cellar deep under living rock, endless rows of towering shelves receding into darkness, stacked with corked glass vessels each holding a tiny living storm - a snow-squall, a small flickering thunderhead, grey rain falling on nothing - paper name-labels hung at their necks, a small lantern-lit party of medieval soldiers and one giantess dwarfed among the shelves, broken storm-glass drifted like frost on the flagstones, utter windless stillness, strictly medieval fantasy - no modern gear, no electric light

a carved stair-lift arch at the end of a forest coursing-lane barred by a single heavy chain, hooded elf archers posted on the stands above it; below the arch an immense queue of ox-drawn grain wagons winding back down a wooded valley out of sight for miles, drovers' fires beside the stalled wheels in evening light; before the chain a small grey-cloaked elf woman lays papers on a trestle table facing three hooded elven elders, strictly medieval - no modern clothing, no firearms

a vast open night-dark shelf-land between two floors, a bare plain running to unseen rims under a starless roof of darkness that is the underside of the country above, a cold wind implied in blown dust and bent lantern flames, great slanting cables going home into black anchor fittings; along a road through the dark a chain of glass-vaulted garden closes each glowing with its own small sky - one in blossom, one full of falling snow - and in the nearest close medieval soldiers mowing ripe barley with scythes by its own warm harvest-evening light, half-built stooks along a hedge, a hooded lantern column of an army waiting quietly on the road, strictly medieval clothing and tools, wrought iron and small glass panes only, no modern greenhouses, no iron hall, no ribs

a court held where a throne once stood: a long scarred wooden trestle table on a vast bare iron floor under a starless black sky, lamplight the only light, one great open ledger and stacked bundles of petitions tied with cord, a lone man in a fine coat standing before a half-ring of gaunt freed folk of many medieval peoples - men, giants, goblins - seated on benches and wagon-boards, a small goblin holding a slate, the dim crowd of a whole world beyond the lamps, the iron floor running out to a distant vanishing point, strictly medieval, no gallows, no modern furniture
